text:
maria: Hey team — saw a p99 jump on hostpool-a starting ~13:42 UTC. Baseline ~18ms, spiking to ~34ms on requests that hit the host-side parse/tokenize path. Only affects streaming HTTP/gRPC ingress. Link to short flame: https://perf.redwood/flare/3101112222

maria: quick log snippet:
```
[13:42:15.123] ingress parse 12.6ms tokenization 9.8ms http2: WINDOW_UPDATE wait
[13:42:15.124] kvcache miss (prefix) -> fallback
```

devon: Was anything deployed around then? kernel/infra changes?

maria: No infra deploys. There was a thin-client tweak rolled out to ~10% at 13:30 but nothing infra. Traffic QPS steady.

sasha: I grabbed a flamegraph from the canary: tokenization & request parsing dominate host CPU now, not decoder. Also seeing extra writev syscalls when streaming chunk boundaries align oddly. https://perf.redwood/graphs/3101112222-flame

jon: Interesting — batching heuristics got worse because request size histogram shifted to many small messages (~<200 tokens) so batching window rarely fills. Kernel selection still prefers f32 path but costs are dominated pre-GPU. Histogram: small requests went from 18% -> 46% in the window.

kevin: Could be KV cache churn too — if prefix KVs are evicted we do extra parse->kv lookups and fallback to full parse. Any spike in KV miss rate?

perf-bot: Automated summary: parse/tokenize time +8.7ms p99 increase; KV miss rate +12% for affected hosts; HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE backpressure observed (burst at 13:42). See /incidents/3101112222.

devon: Quick mitigation: enable lightweight tokenizer fallback flag on canary: `--tokenizer-fast-path=true` — it avoids some allocations for small messages. Can push as hotfix for the affected pool.

maria: Pushed the flag to canary hosts; p99 dropped ~4.2ms within 5m. Looks promising :thumbsup: Should we roll to all hostpool-a?

sasha: Nice. Caveat: fallback increases CPU per-request slightly for large requests and prevents some batching-friendly transforms. If we roll, we should also patch the parser to reuse buffers (avoid early realloc) and add better chunk coalescing on the stream-framer.

jon: Minimal change that helped in my local runs — reuse buffer and avoid copying on boundary: 
```
// reuse buffer
buf.clear(); // keep capacity
read_into(&mut buf)?; // avoid new allocation per chunk
```
Also prefer accumulating until small-slab threshold before a writev to reduce syscall churn.

maria: OK creating ticket and assigning owners. GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/7543 — assigned to @jon and @sasha. Will monitor canary and follow up. If anyone sees regression after wider rollout ping here.

kevin: I'll audit KV eviction policy for prefixes — low-hanging win if we can reduce misses.

perf-bot: Noted. Automated integration will post updated graphs in 10m.

maria: thanks everyone — follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 to decide rollout and perf tests.
